subject: general
question: A sum of money doubled itself at a certain rate of compound interest in 10 years. In how many years will it become eight times?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a **sum of money** becomes 2 times in 10 years at **compound interest**.

Then it becomes 2ⁿ times in n × 10 years.

We need the sum to become 8 times, which is 2³ times.

Here, n = 3, so required time = 3 × 10 = 30 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Principal = P

Amount after 10 years (A₁) = 2P

Target Amount (A₂) = 8P

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d80757dee101edad700bb54c4309481435f9b047d68ef763b5f499d4091c3a96.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2P = P(1 + r/100)¹⁰

⇒ 2 = (1 + r/100)¹⁰

⇒ We need 8P = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ 8 = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ 2³ = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ Substituting the value of 2: [(1 + r/100)¹⁰]³ = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ (1 + r/100)³⁰ = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ t = 30 years

**∴ The correct answer is 30 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Growth

In compound interest, money grows geometrically. If a sum becomes 'k' times in 'T' years, it will become kⁿ times in (n × T) years.

Effective Rate of Interest

The effective annual rate increases when interest is compounded more frequently (half-yearly or quarterly) compared to annually.

Simple Interest Comparison

In Simple Interest, if a sum doubles in 10 years, it means the interest earned is 100% of P in 10 years. To become 8 times (700% interest), it would take 70 years.</p
